title: Prachinburi Mookata 2026 — 8 Great-Value Grill Spots Locals Love
metaDesc: Where locals go for mookata (Thai BBQ) in Prachinburi, Thailand — from 129 THB in-town buffets to riverside grills in Kabin Buri, with areas, rough prices and opening hours, picked from real reviews.
keywords: Prachinburi mookata, Prachinburi Thai BBQ, Prachinburi grill buffet, Kabin Buri mookata
intro: As the afternoon sun softens over Prachinburi, the smell of grilling pork and bubbling broth starts drifting out of shopfronts all over town. Mookata (Thai BBQ on a domed grill) is the dinner locals actually meet friends and bring the family for. We've picked 8 spots that give you good value and fill you up without hurting your wallet — from in-town buffets for around a hundred baht to riverside places over in Kabin Buri.

blocks.html: In Prachinburi, mookata is just a normal weeknight dinner. You'll find everything from cheap all-you-can-eat buffets in town, to set-menu places that keep your budget easy to control, to nicer riverside grills out around Kabin Buri. We've ranked them by value and by which occasion they suit best. The prices listed are rough figures from reviews and can shift with the time of year and the shop's own promotions, so it's worth checking the restaurant's page before you go.

If you're coming as a group and want to eat as much as possible for a fixed price, the hundred-baht buffets in the town center are the best value. Most open from late afternoon until around 10pm, so you can take your time.

items.name: Moo Kratha Khun Ta
items.blurb: All-you-can-eat at about the cheapest price in town. Pork, side dishes and snacks all loaded in for around a hundred baht. It's the spot students and families pick when they want the most for their money. It's near the old bus terminal in the center of town and easy to find.

items.name: Khun Chai Mookata Buffet
items.blurb: Another hundred-baht buffet with no time limit on your table. Easy if you've got small kids along — children up to 100cm tall eat free. Good for families who want to settle in for a long, unhurried dinner.

items.name: Tanyong Mookata Buffet
items.blurb: A buffet with both pork and grilled seafood included at one price, with several kinds of fresh seafood to choose from. Reviewers like getting shrimp and seafood without paying extra per plate. It costs a touch more, but the seafood is what you're getting in return.

blocks.title: Keeping costs down
blocks.html: Plenty of buffets charge for wasted food if you pile up your plate and can't finish it. Take a little at a time and top up — it works out cheaper and saves you the surcharge. Drinks are usually billed separately too, so check before you order a pitcher.

blocks.text: Set-menu spots, easy on the budget

blocks.html: If you're only a couple of people, or you don't eat much, ordering a set is often better value than a buffet because you pay for exactly what you eat. These places lean more on the quality of the meat and the dipping sauce than on sheer quantity.

items.name: Mookata Khon Wang
items.blurb: A set-menu place locals rate among the best for its dipping sauce — bold and punchy in a way that really works with the pork. Sets range from small to jumbo depending on your group size. It's near Robinson, easy to reach with handy parking.
items.meta: Near Robinson, Prachinburi town · open from 3pm

items.name: Phloen Phung–Arunee Mookata (Branch 2)
items.blurb: A riverside spot where you can sit and catch the cool breeze. Beyond the pork, the standout is the old-style glass-noodle salad (yam wun sen) that nearly every table orders. Order one mookata set first and top up the meat as you go — the budget trick reviewers recommend.

items.name: Sudarat Korean Grilled Beef
items.blurb: Beef lovers should try this one — Korean-style grilled beef that's well marinated. A small set is enough for two, and it's perfect for a night you want to swap plain pork for proper grilled beef.

blocks.text: Over in Kabin Buri: riverside grills with good vibes

blocks.html: If you're staying or sightseeing around Kabin Buri, you don't need to drive back into town. This side has grill spots where you can sit by the river in the evening — great for a meal where you want to settle in and chat for a while.

items.name: Tanyong Mookata Kabin Buri
items.blurb: Tanyong's Kabin Buri branch, where the draw is riverside seating with lovely evening light. Reviewers often mention the view and the generous portions, so it's good for a group that wants both the setting and a proper feed.

items.name: 3 Sas Mookata Kabin
items.blurb: A hundred-baht buffet on the Kabin side with Korean-sauce marinated pork, shrimp and fresh seafood all in for one price. It's across from Kabin Chaloemratch Park, and you can book a table ahead if you're coming as a group.
items.meta: Across from Kabin Chaloemratch Park · open daily 3:30pm–10pm

blocks.title: Heading to Kabin Buri for dinner
blocks.html: Riverside spots on the Kabin side fill up fast on Friday and Saturday. If you're coming as a group, call ahead to book a riverside table and you'll land a better spot than walking in. Arrive before sunset and you'll get to sit and watch the evening light.

blocks.text: How to eat Prachinburi mookata for the best value

items: Coming as a group? Go buffet — for four or more, the hundred-baht buffets usually beat ordering sets, since you keep eating for the same fixed price.
Just two of you? Order a set — pay for what you actually eat. Start with a small set and top up the meat, rather than committing to a buffet you'll leave half-finished.
Want seafood? Pick a combined grilled-seafood spot — some places fold shrimp and seafood into a single buffet price, which beats ordering seafood plate by plate.
Go early evening — popular spots fill up fast after 6pm. Get there earlier for a good table and no queue.

blocks.html: One more thing locals do is check the shop's page for promos first. Many places run weekday deals or big-group discounts that aren't posted out front — just ask the staff when you book.

faq.q: Which mookata spot in Prachinburi is the cheapest?
faq.a: The hundred-baht buffets in town like Moo Kratha Khun Ta and Khun Chai start at around 129 THB per person, all-you-can-eat — the best-value option if you're with a few people. Prices can shift with the shop's promotions, so check their page before you head over.

faq.q: Where should I go for riverside grilling in Prachinburi?
faq.a: The Kabin Buri side has several riverside spots, like Tanyong Mookata's Kabin branch with its lovely evening light, and 3 Sas Mookata across from Kabin Chaloemratch Park. They're great for settling in and catching the cool breeze. Book a riverside table ahead on Friday or Saturday.

faq.q: What time do mookata restaurants in Prachinburi open?
faq.a: Most open from late afternoon into the evening, around 3–4pm, and close around 10pm — they're mainly a dinner thing. To get a good table without a queue, go early evening before 6pm.

faq.q: Is a set or a buffet better value?
faq.a: It depends on your group. For four or more who eat a lot, the hundred-baht buffets usually win. But for two people, or if you don't eat much, ordering a small set and topping up the meat means you pay for what you actually eat and end up spending less.

faq.q: Do Prachinburi mookata spots have seafood?
faq.a: Yes — several do combined grilled seafood in a single buffet price, like Tanyong Mookata with both pork and seafood, and 3 Sas with shrimp and fresh seafood. If you like seafood, these spots are better value than ordering it plate by plate.
